rules_for_every_task: Project root C:/Dev/squad-ai/Brainstorming/games/out_of_sight (namespace OutOfSight, Unity 6.3 URP). Read LEVELS_V2.md sections 1, 2, 4 and your own section before starting.

Use the PowerShell tool, never Git Bash. Unity only through the lock wrapper: pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/unity.ps1 -Agent <task id> -UnityArgs "...". Never kill another Unity process; the lock may be busy (other agents queue on it).
Edit only your owner_files (plus new files you create under the paths named in your instructions). If you need a change in a file you do not own, write it in your report for the owner.
No git write commands. English in code, comments and docs. Never the em-dash character anywhere (code, strings, JSON, docs).

A parallel visual-polish workflow has uncommitted edits in SaveData.cs, Tuning.cs, Hud.cs, LevelBuilder.cs, Robot.cs, GardenBackdrop.cs, Menu.cs, GhostView.cs, OrbitCamera.cs and others: edit on top of them, never revert them.
Every new LevelDef field needs C1 first: LevelJson uses MissingMemberHandling.Error, so a level file with an unknown key fails to load.
Audit messages stay in French (existing convention). Every new rule gets a MUTATION tag comment; list the tag and the mutation.sh line you propose in your report (I1 owns mutation.sh).

Compile check: pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/unity.ps1 -Agent <id> -UnityArgs "run . --timeout 1800 -- -executeMethod OutOfSight.Editor.Builder.SetupAndCompile -logFile Build/<id>_compile.log". EditMode tests: -UnityArgs "test . --mode EditMode --report-format junit --output TestResults/<id>_edit.xml --timeout 3000". PlayMode tests: -UnityArgs "test . --mode PlayMode --filter <names> --report-format junit --output TestResults/<id>_play.xml --timeout 3000".

Audit a level: -UnityArgs "run . --timeout 3000 -- -executeMethod OutOfSight.Editor.LevelAudit.RunBatch -auditLevels <ids or absolute paths without .json> -skipFixtures -difficulty normal,difficile -slack -strictRooms -json Build/levels_v2/<id>.json -logFile Build/<id>.log" (-strictRooms and -json exist after C5). -writeRoutes only on files under Assets, only once the targets hold (LEVELS_V2 4.5).
Finish with a report (your final message): what changed, the numbers asked by your acceptance, test premises you broke (file, test, why), proposed mutation lines, open problems.

tasks.title: Schema v2: new level and manifest fields with validation
tasks.instructions: Spec: LEVELS_V2.md section 6 (row C1), wave1/code_features.json (features 'Progression v2', 'requires', 'Lit zones', 'Door only an inhabitant opens', 'Night lighting preset', 'Routine authoring: periodic glances', 'Audit: via checks', 'Record revision'). Data model and validation ONLY, no runtime or audit behaviour. Add to LevelDef (all optional, omitted from serialization when default, DefaultValueHandling.Ignore pattern): int Rev ('rev', >= 0) and RecordId => Rev > 0 ? Id + "~" + Rev : Id; List<string> RequiredLessons with [JsonProperty("requires")] (the name Requires would clash with the static LevelDef.Lessons naming); PaceDef Pace ('pace': minShare, maxShare, minPauses, maxPause, every key optional); List<ViaCheckDef> ViaChecks ('viaChecks': name, x, z, sizeX, sizeZ, maxRatio default 1.5, avoid bool); List<LitZoneDef> LitZones ('litZones': name, x, z, sizeX, sizeZ, max 4); string Lighting ('lighting': 'day' default or 'night'). OpeningDef: bool PlayerLocked ('playerLocked'). StationDef: GlanceEveryDef GlanceEvery ('glanceEvery': start, period, hold, yaw, alternate, count optional) expanded into Glances in LevelJson.Parse right after deserialization (merged and sorted with explicit glances, like ResolveSeats); ShouldSerializeGlances false when every glance was generated. New lesson ids accepted in 'requires' (and as 'lesson' where meaningful): rug, hum, contact, household, decoy, exitwatch, lit, plus every existing lesson id. Manifest: keep LevelManifest.Parse(json) -> List<string>; add ParseFull(json) -> ManifestDef { int Rev = 1; List<string> Levels; List<string> Previous; List<ActDef> Acts (from, nameKey) }. Validator issues: rev < 0; unknown requires id; requires prerequisites (hum/contact need a robot; household a leaf with openedByInhabitants; decoy a decoy of the player's kind; lit litZones and a floor lamp body; exitwatch an exit; pet a dog; wardrobe a wardrobe the body fits; door a closed leaf the player may open; rug a rug or soft room); at most 5 requires ids; pace ranges (0 <= minShare <= maxShare <= 1, minPauses >= 0, 0 < maxPause <= Tuning.AuditMaxWait); viaChecks inside a room, unique names, at most 2; litZones inside one room, not overlapping the exit, at most 4, issue if the body is not the floor lamp; lighting known; playerLocked needs leaf 'closed' and openedByInhabitants true; glanceEvery: period >= hold + 2 x (0.6 + |yaw|/200), |yaw| <= 80, start + count x period <= dwell, not on a dog. Do not edit any level file other than new test fixtures. Keep it small and land it first: every other task waits on it.
acceptance: Project compiles (SetupAndCompile log without errors).

EditMode suite green, including new LevelDefV2Tests: parse and round-trip of every new field (compact form kept for glanceEvery); glanceEvery expansion equals a fixture copy of level18 Odile's current hand-written 34 glances (period 9, hold 5, yaw -80); each validator rule has one passing and one failing case; ParseFull reads rev, previous, acts and Parse still returns the list.
All 24 existing level files and title_house.json still load and validate unchanged.

tasks.title: Progression v2: manifest rev 2, unlock rule, save migration, record revision, level select
owner_files: Assets/Tests/EditMode/CoreM5Tests.cs (unlock test only; T1 takes the file over later)
tasks.instructions: Spec: LEVELS_V2.md section 7 and wave1/code_features.json features 'Progression v2', 'Record revision per redesigned level', 'Level select for the v2 line-up'. (1) levels.json: {"rev": 2, "previous": [level1..level24 in v1 order], "levels": [level1, level2, level3, level4, level5, level6, level7, level8, level9, level12, level11, level15, level13, level14, level18, level17, level19, level21, level20, level22, level24], "acts": [{from 0, act1.name}, {from 7, act2.name}, {from 16, act3.name}]} (21 entries: LV12 inserts level25 between level22 and level24 later). (2) LevelLoader.LoadManifestDef(). (3) SaveData: [JsonProperty("unlocked")] List<string> Unlocked (missing = empty, wrong type = parse problem like 'won'); [JsonProperty("order")] int Order (missing or < 1 = 1); version stays 1. IsUnlocked(order, i) = valid index && (i == 0 || Won has order[i] || Won has order[i-1] || Unlocked has order[i]). MigrateOrder(rev, previous, current) -> bool: if Order >= rev nothing; else every previous[j] playable under the old rule (j == 0 or previous[j-1] won) and listed in current joins Unlocked, then Order = rev. Never removes anything from Won or Best. (4) SaveStore.Load calls it after a successful parse; when it returns true, save with the existing atomic write and log '[SaveStore] progress migrated to order rev 2: +N unlocked'. (5) Records: RecordWin(levelId, recordId, seconds, difficulty) adds levelId to Won and stores the time under DifficultyDef.RecordKey(recordId, difficulty); RecordLine passes game.Def.RecordId; LevelSelect reads best times with the card's RecordId (LevelMiniature already parses each level). (6) LevelSelect: default selection = the card of SaveStore.FirstUnwonLevel; an act tag ('Acte 2' from the act nameKey via Strings) on the first card of each act. Strings keys act1.name/act2.name/act3.name are written by S1; use Strings lookups only. (7) Tests: rewrite CoreM5Tests.IsUnlocked_opens_a_level_once_the_one_before_it_is_won (line ~1833 asserts a won level is locked, contrary to the new rule); SaveM5Tests: the four worked cases of section 7, fresh save, idempotent second load (no write), wrong-typed 'unlocked' rejected, missing 'order' reads 1, Won and Best never shrink; DifficultyM7Tests: RecordKey with a rev id ('level6~1@difficile'), an old bare 'level6' record not shown for a rev 1 level6 while Won still has 'level6'; ProbeTestsM5Ui: a step where a migrated save opens the expected cards and the act tags show. Mutation tags UNLOCK_WON, UNLOCK_MIGRATED, MIGRATE_PREDECESSOR.
acceptance: Compiles; EditMode suite green except tests T1 owns that fail only because of the new order (list them in the report).
New and rewritten tests in CoreM5Tests (unlock), SaveM5Tests, DifficultyM7Tests green.
PlayMode: pwsh ... test . --mode PlayMode --filter Step41 green including the new step.

tasks.instructions: Spec: wave1/code_features.json features 'Start on first input (held start)' and 'Door only an inhabitant opens'. Held start: GameState.Started; BuildLevel sets Started = !HoldStart. While !Started, FixedUpdate only reads input: no furniture motion, inhabitants, robots, vision, creak or Steps; rigs keep their idle pose. The first step with a move input above the dead zone or the action key sets Started and runs in full (step 1 of the schedule). Camera input and the careful key alone do not start. Pause works while held; restart and next level hold again. static HoldStart default true in the player and editor play mode, false when Probe.Requested or SaveStore.IsTestRun (existing tests keep t0 = build). Elapsed counts from the release (records exclude card time). Expose an event or property the HUD (C3b) can read. RouteReplayer: Game.ReleaseStart() called at the first sample when a test turns the hold on. Player-locked leaf: ClaimActionKey skips a closed leaf with PlayerLocked (no action begins); expose a query (e.g. GameState.LockedLeafInReach) so the HUD can show 'Locked'. MUTATION tags HOLD_START, LOCKED_LEAF. Do not touch Hud.cs (C3b).
acceptance: Compiles; EditMode suite green.

New ProbeTestsHeldStart green: held 3 s with no input gives Steps == 0, every routine at its start pose, creak 0, robot not moved; the first move input starts the level; a designer route replayed with the hold on and ReleaseStart at sample 0 wins on the same exit step as with the hold off (level1 and level8); E next to a playerLocked leaf does nothing while a household walk still opens it (fixture level).

tasks.title: Audit A: pace metrics and gate, dead rooms, JSON report, flicker collapse, walk-line and dark checks
tasks.instructions: Spec: LEVELS_V2.md 1.3 (definitions) and section 6 row C5; wave1/code_features.json 'Audit: pace metrics, dead rooms and a JSON report' and 'Audit: collapse in-place toggle runs'. (1) Pace from the found path: travel = cell moves x the body's cell cost (+ office chair glide, + rocking chair rock counted as travel); waiting = exit - travel; in-place actions (toggle, door open, hide, hidden time, leave) count as waiting; pinned (sat on) time reported apart and excluded from the share's denominator. Pauses = runs of >= 5 samples at one cell; MidPauses exclude the run starting at t = 0; LongestPause. Print 'rythme : attente X s (Y %), N pauses (M en route), plus longue Z s, assis dessus P s' at every difficulty. The level 'pace' field: outside it at Normal = failure 'rythme hors cible : ...'; at Difficile = note. (2) Dead rooms: used when the path or a via path has a cell in it, a station or robot waypoint lies in it, any inhabitant position sample lies in it, or a wardrobe in it is used; else 'AVERTISSEMENT piece morte : <id>'; -strictRooms makes it a failure. (3) -json <file>: per level and difficulty {id, exit, travel, waitShare, pauses, midPauses, longestPause, pinned, slack, margin, deadRooms[], lessons{id: binds}, requires{}, vias{}, budgets{drawCalls, materials}, habitWarnings[]}. (4) Route post-process: an even run of back-to-back toggles at one cell becomes a wait, an odd run a single toggle at its last time; a hide immediately followed by a leave (hidden < 0.5 s) is removed when the route without it still passes; keep the collapsed route only if FidelityReplay passes, else keep the original with 'clignotement conserve'. (5) Warning 'AVERTISSEMENT pause sur un trajet : ...' when a route pause (>= 0.5 s) lies within 0.6 m of an inhabitant walk segment while that inhabitant walks it. (6) Dark check synchronised: replace or complement DarkFreePass with 'some memory watcher has the lamp within its dark range and inside its cone at the same sample, before the exit'; print the time and distance. Fixtures (validating, small): one pace pass, one pace fail, one empty room, one toggle flicker. Do not implement requires/vias (C6). Do not change the search itself beyond the post-process.
acceptance: Compiles; EditMode green.
Fixture run: -executeMethod OutOfSight.Editor.LevelAudit.RunBatch -fixtures (or -auditLevels on the new fixtures) reports the expected pass/fail for each new fixture.

Audit of level6,level20,level22 at normal,difficile with -json: prints the rythme line, writes the JSON, level20's designerRoute toggles collapse to 1, level22's 0.0 s hide/leave pairs disappear or are flagged, level3 prints the walk-line warning (current data), and the exit times of the 24 current levels are unchanged (spot-check 1, 13, 24).

(2) viaChecks: Search with MustVisit = the zone's cells (one Visit bit in the node key), failure 'aucun horaire par <name>', warning when the via exit > maxRatio x best exit; avoid = true bars the zone instead and the route must not exist or must be slower. Via paths count as used for dead rooms. JSON report gets requires{} and vias{} filled. (3) Player-locked leaves: no Reach cells or ReachBits for the player; failure 'porte verrouillee jamais ouverte' when no household walk opens it. (4) Lit cells: World.Lit[cell]; after ComputeSight and before dilation, copy MoveSeen into MoveDark and Seen into SeenDark for lit cells; FidelityReplay uses the full range when the centre is lit; DarkFreePass ignores lit cells; note 'echantillons en zone eclairee : N'. Keep requires to at most 5 extra searches. MUTATION tags REQUIRES_BIND, VIA_MUSTVISIT.

tasks.instructions: Spec: wave1/code_features.json 'Rush counter-route probe over every listed level'. Data-driven PlayMode step over levels.json at Normal, [Category("Slow")].
